description: Real skills for tough moments — breathing, grounding, movement, self-talk.

1.definition: In 4, hold 4, out 4, hold 4. A reset button for big feelings.
1.scenarioDoneTo: Heart racing before a big test.
1.scenarioYouDo: Heart racing before a big test.

challenge.scenario: Racing heart, 30 seconds to reset. Best move?
options: Box breathe: in 4, hold 4, out 4, hold 4.
Panic a lot more and stew in it.
Hold your breath till you calm down.

2.definition: A slow, boxed breath that turns on the calm system.
2.scenarioDoneTo: About to walk on stage for a debate.
2.scenarioYouDo: About to walk on stage for a debate.

challenge.scenario: Tight chest, seconds before going on. Best?
options: Box breathe backstage: 3 slow cycles right now.
Chug a giant energy drink real fast.
Convince yourself you aren't nervous at all.

2.tip: The exhale is the calming part. Extend it.

3.definition: Structured breathing that lowers cortisol reactivity.
3.scenarioDoneTo: Two minutes before a hard performance review.
3.scenarioYouDo: Two minutes before a hard performance review.

challenge.scenario: Two minutes to regulate. Best pre-game move?
options: 5 rounds of box breathing to drop the arousal.
Rehearse your defense while pacing the whole hall.
Skip breathing, just run on the adrenaline high.

1.definition: Notice 5 sights, 4 touches, 3 sounds, 2 smells, 1 taste.
1.scenarioDoneTo: Big wave of worry at recess.
1.scenarioYouDo: Big wave of worry at recess.

challenge.scenario: Worry hits hard. What helps you land?
options: 5 see, 4 touch, 3 hear, 2 smell, 1 taste.
Just hide and hope the worry passes.
Panic even harder about the whole thing.

1.tip: Grounding brings your brain back to your body.

2.definition: A sensory tool that interrupts anxious thought loops.
2.scenarioDoneTo: Spiraling in your head at lunch.
2.scenarioYouDo: Spiraling in your head at lunch.

challenge.scenario: Spiraling. How do you re-enter the room?
options: Silently walk through 5-4-3-2-1 to re-anchor.
Fake attention and keep on spiraling anyway.
Excuse yourself and go spiral alone somewhere.

2.tip: You can't be worrying AND in your senses at once.

challenge.scenario: Dissociating in a meeting. Discreet grounding?
options: Feet on floor, 5 objects, 3 sounds, one texture.
Push through, ignore the disconnection completely.
Get up and just leave without saying a word.

3.tip: Sensory grounding is the fastest way back.

1.definition: Splash cold water on your face. A body reset.
1.scenarioDoneTo: You're about to explode after arguing with your sibling.
1.scenarioYouDo: You're about to explode after arguing with your sibling.

challenge.scenario: Big anger. What resets your body fast?
options: Splash cold water on your face for 30 seconds.
Just yell way more at your sibling right now.
Break something to get all the anger out.

1.tip: Cold on your face triggers a calming reflex.

2.definition: Cold triggers the dive reflex and slows your heart.
2.scenarioDoneTo: Crying so hard you can't catch your breath.
2.scenarioYouDo: Crying so hard you can't catch your breath.

challenge.scenario: Sobbing, breath won't slow. Fast reset?
options: Cold water on face plus slow long exhales.
Try to argue back through all the tears somehow.
Hold your breath as hard as you can to stop.

2.tip: Cold on face lowers nervous-system overdrive fast.

3.definition: DBT distress skill: temperature to reduce activation.
3.scenarioDoneTo: In emotional crisis, can't think clearly.
3.scenarioYouDo: In emotional crisis, can't think clearly.

challenge.scenario: Crisis mode. Talk therapy won't stick yet. First?
options: Regulate the body first: cold, exhale, then talk.
Try to reason through it while dysregulated anyway.
Skip the body, go straight into problem-solving mode.

1.definition: Big feelings need somewhere to go. Move them.
1.scenarioDoneTo: SO frustrated with homework, you want to rip it.
1.scenarioYouDo: SO frustrated with homework, you want to rip it.

challenge.scenario: Frustration peaking. Healthy release?
options: Do 20 jumping jacks, then come right back.
Just rip the homework into a bunch of pieces.
Sit right there and stew in the anger.

1.tip: Feelings are physical. Move to move them.

2.definition: Movement burns off stress chemicals fast.
2.scenarioDoneTo: Wired with nervous energy before a big audition.
2.scenarioYouDo: Wired with nervous energy before a big audition.

challenge.scenario: Nervous energy, big moment coming. What helps?
options: 5-minute brisk walk to burn off the surplus.
Sit still and try to force yourself calm somehow.
Chug an energy drink for even more adrenaline.

2.tip: Adrenaline is fuel. Give it a place to burn.

3.definition: Aerobic movement is real medicine for anxiety.
3.scenarioDoneTo: Depressed for a week. Bed feels like the only option.
3.scenarioYouDo: Depressed for a week. Bed feels like the only option.

challenge.scenario: Depression is heavy. Smallest useful move?
options: Get outside for 10 minutes of slow walking.
Wait to 'feel better' before you move at all.
Just keep scrolling on your phone in bed.

cards.name: Talk to Yourself Like a Friend

1.definition: Talk to yourself the way you'd talk to a friend.
1.scenarioDoneTo: You slipped up in class. Inner voice is mean.
1.scenarioYouDo: You slipped up in class. Inner voice is mean.

challenge.scenario: Cruel inner voice after a slip. Better move?
options: 'That was hard. You're okay. Still learning.'
Keep beating yourself up over the mistake.
Tell yourself you are literally the worst.

1.tip: Give yourself what you'd give a friend.

2.definition: Notice it's hard, offer yourself some kindness.
2.scenarioDoneTo: You bombed a test after studying hard.
2.scenarioYouDo: You bombed a test after studying hard.

challenge.scenario: Spiraling on 'not smart enough.' Self-compassion move?
options: 'This is hard. I can be kind to myself here.'
'I really am not smart enough for any of this.'
'I'll just punish myself into doing better next time.'

3.definition: Neff's break: this is hard, others feel this too, be kind.
3.scenarioDoneTo: Big professional mistake. Inner court in session.
3.scenarioYouDo: Big professional mistake. Inner court in session.

challenge.scenario: Inner critic at full volume. Reframe?
options: 'This is suffering. Others too. Be kind now.'
'I deserve every bit of the self-attack coming.'
'Work harder so I never feel this way again ever.'

1.definition: Write the thought. Ask 'is it true?'
1.scenarioDoneTo: 'Nobody likes me' keeps looping after one bad day.
1.scenarioYouDo: 'Nobody likes me' keeps looping after one bad day.

challenge.scenario: 'Nobody likes me' won't stop. Useful step?
options: Write it down. Ask: 'Is that really true?'
Just believe the thought as full solid fact.
Ignore it and hope it goes away by itself.

2.definition: Situation → thought → feeling → evidence → balanced view.
2.scenarioDoneTo: 'I'm going to fail this class' loops all week.
2.scenarioYouDo: 'I'm going to fail this class' loops all week.

challenge.scenario: 'I'll fail' on loop. Real intervention?
options: Thought record: catch, test, build a balanced view.
Try to just think positive without any evidence.
Accept the thought as the plain honest truth.

2.tip: A thought record slows the reactive brain down.

3.definition: Cognitive restructuring. The core CBT skill.
3.scenarioDoneTo: 'I'm not competent' fires before every meeting.
3.scenarioYouDo: 'I'm not competent' fires before every meeting.

challenge.scenario: Chronic self-critical thought. CBT tool?
options: Thought record: test evidence, build a counter.
Just try really hard to suppress the whole thought.
Overprepare each time to prove the thought wrong.

3.tip: Chronic thoughts need chronic practice. Reps.

1.definition: When you don't feel like it, do it anyway.
1.scenarioDoneTo: Bummed. Friend invites you to the park.
1.scenarioYouDo: Bummed. Friend invites you to the park.

challenge.scenario: Don't feel like going. Healthy move?
options: Say yes even if you don't feel like it.
Wait until you feel better to do anything fun.
Cancel because your mood is currently saying no.

1.tip: Feelings follow action. Mood catches up.

2.definition: Doing valued things gently lifts mood over time.
2.scenarioDoneTo: In a slump. Nothing feels fun anymore.
2.scenarioYouDo: In a slump. Nothing feels fun anymore.

challenge.scenario: Nothing feels fun. Intervention?
options: Schedule one small thing you used to enjoy.
Wait for the motivation to just come back on its own.
Keep avoiding until you eventually feel better again.

2.tip: Depression lies about how it will feel.

3.scenarioDoneTo: Depression pulled you off exercise and social life.
3.scenarioYouDo: Depression pulled you off exercise and social life.

challenge.scenario: Motivation feels dead. Intervention?
options: Schedule 1-2 small mastery activities each day.
Wait for the depression to lift on its own instead.
Push for one huge overhaul of everything at once.

3.tip: Motivation is a byproduct of action.

1.definition: Sleep is when your brain cleans up feelings.
1.scenarioDoneTo: It's 11pm. You want to keep scrolling.
1.scenarioYouDo: It's 11pm. You want to keep scrolling.

challenge.scenario: Late night, phone in hand. Healthy move?
options: Put the phone down. Tomorrow-you will thank you.
Just keep scrolling for one more little hour.
Stay up all night, deal with it in the morning.

2.definition: Consistent sleep timing protects mood and focus.
2.scenarioDoneTo: Sleeping different times every night lately.
2.scenarioYouDo: Sleeping different times every night lately.

challenge.scenario: Scattered sleep, everything harder. First move?
options: Anchor a bedtime and wake time. Weekends too.
Sleep in every single day to catch up on the debt.
Just push through the rest of it with more caffeine.

2.tip: Consistency matters more than total hours.

3.definition: Sleep debt directly worsens anxiety and depression.

challenge.scenario: Chronic under-sleep. What's the intervention?
options: Treat sleep as a first-order fix. Do it first.
Take on even more caffeine to keep pushing through.
Assume the mood and memory issues are separate.

3.tip: Sleep is the highest-leverage mental-health input.

1.definition: Write every worry down. Quieter than in your head.
1.scenarioDoneTo: Can't sleep. Worries won't stop about tomorrow.
1.scenarioYouDo: Can't sleep. Worries won't stop about tomorrow.

challenge.scenario: Mind won't stop at bedtime. What helps?
options: Grab paper. Write it all out for 5 minutes.
Just lie there and keep worrying about it all.
Check your phone to distract yourself for a while.

1.tip: Paper gives worries a place to live.

2.definition: Free-writing worries moves them out of the loop.
2.scenarioDoneTo: Exam prep to do. Random anxieties won't stop.
2.scenarioYouDo: Exam prep to do. Random anxieties won't stop.

challenge.scenario: Anxious thoughts block your studying. Move?
options: Brain-dump for 10 minutes, THEN study clearer.
Just study while distracted and hope for the best.
Give up on studying and doom-scroll for a while.

3.scenarioDoneTo: Days out from a major decision. Head full of loops.
3.scenarioYouDo: Days out from a major decision. Head full of loops.

challenge.scenario: Loops before a big decision. Tool?
options: Write the loop. Extract known / fear / action.
Just keep looping in your head, hope it clears.
Decide impulsively so you can end the whole loop.

1.definition: Ask 'what kind of person do I want to be?'
1.scenarioDoneTo: You want to say something mean.
1.scenarioYouDo: You want to say something mean.

challenge.scenario: Mean words on the tip of your tongue. Check?
options: 'Being a good friend matters. Not this.'
Just go ahead and say the mean thing anyway.
Ghost the friend right now without saying it.

1.tip: Feelings pass. Who you're becoming lasts.

2.definition: Let your values steer, not your immediate mood.
2.scenarioDoneTo: You said you'd volunteer. Not in the mood.
2.scenarioYouDo: You said you'd volunteer. Not in the mood.

challenge.scenario: Commitment vs. bad mood. Values move?
options: 'Being reliable matters. Go, let value pull.'
Just cancel it because you don't feel like going.
Show up but sulk about it the whole entire time.

2.tip: Values are steadier than moods. Let them steer.

3.definition: ACT skill: choose values over mood-driven action.
3.scenarioDoneTo: Anxiety blocks applying for a values-aligned role.
3.scenarioYouDo: Anxiety blocks applying for a values-aligned role.

challenge.scenario: Anxiety blocks a values-aligned move. ACT move?
options: Take the values action, carry anxiety with you.
Wait until anxiety is gone (which may never happen).
Choose the low-anxiety option instead, ignore values.

3.tip: Anxiety and action can coexist. Values move you.

1.definition: Asking a trusted adult isn't weak. It's smart.
1.scenarioDoneTo: Someone at school is being mean every day.
1.scenarioYouDo: Someone at school is being mean every day.

challenge.scenario: Daily mean stuff. Scared to tell. Healthy?
options: Tell a trusted adult. You don't handle it alone.
Handle it entirely by yourself no matter what.
Pretend it isn't happening and hope it stops soon.

1.tip: Real strength knows when to ask for backup.

2.definition: Reaching out is a skill, not a failure.
2.scenarioDoneTo: Having really dark thoughts. Nobody knows.
2.scenarioYouDo: Having really dark thoughts. Nobody knows.

challenge.scenario: Dark thoughts, told no one. Move?
options: Tell a trusted adult. Or call/text 988 today.
Keep it inside and just handle it by yourself.
Deal with it entirely on your own from now on.

3.scenarioDoneTo: Months of managing serious anxiety alone.
3.scenarioYouDo: Months of managing serious anxiety alone.

challenge.scenario: Solo-managing for months. Reframe?
options: Schedule a therapist. Expert help is a skill.
Just keep white-knuckling through it on your own.
Wait until it becomes a full crisis before acting.

3.tip: Therapy is a skill investment, like a coach.

1.definition: Big urges peak fast, then shrink. Ride them out.
1.scenarioDoneTo: HUGE urge to yell mid-argument with a parent.
1.scenarioYouDo: HUGE urge to yell mid-argument with a parent.

challenge.scenario: Huge urge to yell. Healthy move?
options: Wait 60 seconds and breathe. Urge peak passes.
Just yell all of it out right now, in that moment.
Storm off and slam a door hard on the way out.

1.tip: Urges are waves. Ride, don't act.

2.definition: Watch an urge without acting on it. Weakens it.
2.scenarioDoneTo: Strong urge to text an ex who's bad for you.
2.scenarioYouDo: Strong urge to text an ex who's bad for you.

challenge.scenario: Urge to send something you'd regret. Practice?
options: Rate the urge 1-10. Wait 20 min. Watch it change.
Just send it right now and see what happens after.
Suppress it and pretend you feel fine about it.

3.definition: Mindful surfing decouples craving from action.
3.scenarioDoneTo: Recovering. A heavy craving just hit hard.
3.scenarioYouDo: Recovering. A heavy craving just hit hard.

challenge.scenario: Craving hits mid-recovery. Skill?
options: Sit with it. Describe it. Breathe. Watch it pass.
Just give in this one time and start over tomorrow.
White-knuckle it in silence and don't tell anyone.

3.tip: The craving is not you. Watch it pass.

1.definition: Do the OPPOSITE of what the feeling wants.
1.scenarioDoneTo: Sad. You want to hide in your room all day.
1.scenarioYouDo: Sad. You want to hide in your room all day.

challenge.scenario: Sadness says 'hide.' Opposite action?
options: Open curtains. Go outside. One small social thing.
Just hide in your room all day like it wants.
Scroll in bed until the whole feeling passes.

1.tip: Feelings pull toward avoidance. Push back.

2.definition: When a feeling is out of proportion, act opposite.
2.scenarioDoneTo: Shame after a small mistake. Want to disappear.
2.scenarioYouDo: Shame after a small mistake. Want to disappear.

challenge.scenario: Shame says 'disappear.' Opposite action?
options: Stay visible. Talk. Keep eye contact. Engage.
Just hide as the shame is telling you to do.
Overapologize and grovel to everyone all day.

2.tip: Half-doing feeds the feeling. Full opposite works.

3.definition: DBT: regulate unjustified emotions by acting opposite.
3.scenarioDoneTo: Anxiety says skip a networking event good for goals.
3.scenarioYouDo: Anxiety says skip a networking event good for goals.

challenge.scenario: Anxiety says 'skip.' Actually good for you. Move?
options: Attend fully engaged. Not skip. Not half-in.
Just skip it because anxiety told you to skip.
Show up but hide in a corner all night long.

3.tip: Full opposite is where the change lives.

1.definition: Feeling Brain and Thinking Brain working together.
1.scenarioDoneTo: Feelings say quit soccer. Logic says don't.
1.scenarioYouDo: Feelings say quit soccer. Logic says don't.

challenge.scenario: Feelings quit, thoughts stay. Wise mind?
options: 'Frustrated AND love it. Take a break, don't quit.'
Just quit soccer entirely, right now, no going back.
Ignore all your feelings and stay no matter what.

2.definition: Where intuition meets logic. Better decisions live here.
2.scenarioDoneTo: Emotion says text an ex. Logic says don't.
2.scenarioYouDo: Emotion says text an ex. Logic says don't.

challenge.scenario: Emotion says text. Logic says no. Wise?
options: 'I miss them AND texting hurts. Write, don't send.'
Text them right now without thinking about it.
Just suppress the whole feeling and move on today.

2.tip: Wise mind honors both. Acts on neither alone.

3.definition: Integrated state. Values-aligned action lives here.
3.scenarioDoneTo: Career pivot. Emotions and logic disagree.
3.scenarioYouDo: Career pivot. Emotions and logic disagree.

challenge.scenario: Emotion vs. logic on a pivot. Wise approach?
options: Slow down. Listen to both. Find the third option.
Just go with pure emotion and see what happens.
Go with pure logic and ignore the feeling entirely.

3.tip: Wise decisions integrate. Neither voice loses.

1.definition: Give worries a time slot. 'Not now — see you at 5.'
1.scenarioDoneTo: Worrying about a trip while trying to focus in class.
1.scenarioYouDo: Worrying about a trip while trying to focus in class.

challenge.scenario: Worry interrupts class. Move?
options: 'I'll worry at 5pm for 10 minutes. Not now.'
Just worry about the whole thing all day long.
Try to force yourself to never think about it.

1.tip: Worries push harder when told 'no.' Give a time.

2.definition: Postpone worries to a daily 15-min window.
2.scenarioDoneTo: Anxious thoughts pull focus during work and hangs.
2.scenarioYouDo: Anxious thoughts pull focus during work and hangs.

challenge.scenario: Anxiety hijacks focus all day. Technique?
options: Daily 15-min 'worry window.' Postpone the rest.
Just try to stop worrying entirely all the time.
Worry as much as it demands, right when it hits.

3.scenarioDoneTo: General anxiety keeps you in constant low-grade worry.
3.scenarioYouDo: General anxiety keeps you in constant low-grade worry.

challenge.scenario: Constant low-grade worry. Structured tool?
options: Daily worry appointment. Postpone. Stick to it.
Just try to think happy thoughts on demand instead.
Suppress worry whenever it comes up during the day.

3.tip: Worry loves ambiguity. Structure defeats it.

1.definition: Notice 3 good things before bed. Tiny counts.
1.scenarioDoneTo: Rough day. Brain stuck on what went wrong.
1.scenarioYouDo: Rough day. Brain stuck on what went wrong.

challenge.scenario: Brain stuck on negatives. What helps balance?
options: List 3 good things from today. Even tiny ones.
Just focus on what went wrong the entire day.
Skip the whole bedtime routine and stay upset.

1.tip: You see what you practice. Practice good.

2.scenarioDoneTo: Low mood for weeks. Waiting on a therapy appointment.
2.scenarioYouDo: Low mood for weeks. Waiting on a therapy appointment.

challenge.scenario: Waiting on therapy. Small daily practice?
options: Nightly 3-good-things journal for two whole weeks.
Just wait passively for therapy without doing anything.
Ruminate on how bad you feel to really process it.

2.tip: One of the most tested positive practices.

3.definition: Documented mood benefits with sustained practice.
3.scenarioDoneTo: Chronic dissatisfaction despite a good life.
3.scenarioYouDo: Chronic dissatisfaction despite a good life.

challenge.scenario: Chronic negativity bias. Retraining tool?
options: Nightly 3-good-things plus 'why.' Weeks of it.
Just force yourself to feel grateful on command.
Ignore the pattern and hope it fixes on its own.

3.tip: Attention is trainable. Practice reshapes it.
